items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The best example of that you got was Johnny St. Cyr and the Hot Five records and later on with Count Basie’s band, Freddie Guy, or Freddie Green.

ctx.x: You were telling me that you joined Willie Pajeaud’s band, and you played at a place on Canal Street above where the Woolworth’s is.

El Alamo. A dime a dance. Worked there two years with him. 1927. No, not that long. A year and a half, ’til 1928. Then I fooled around with Lee Collins for a year, for around about, that went a year, ’29, and then things is real rough. No work and et cetera. I played in little joints all around. I learned to be a musician, trying to be a musician, which was hard. Everybody had day jobs or they work in the building trades. Whole families was plasterers and bricklayers. Whole families was cigarmakers. Other family…
